message.text: Reactions are removed by explicit Go code during user deletion across all three drivers. The schema is being checked for a foreign key cascade on reaction.creator_id.

Explicit Go code removes emoji reactions during user deletion. The function `deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx` handles reactions on the user's memos.

`deleteReactionsByCreatorTx` removes reactions created by the user. This logic exists in all three database drivers: `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go`, `store/db/mysql/user_delete.go`, and `store/db/postgres/user_delete.go`. The schema contains no foreign key or ON DELETE CASCADE constraint on the reaction table.

explicit Go code; `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go`, `store/db/mysql/user_delete.go`, `store/db/postgres/user_delete.go` (`deleteReactionsByCreatorTx`, `deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx`); schema has no FK/CASCADE (`store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql`, `store/migration/mysql/LATEST.sql`, `store/migration/postgres/LATEST.sql`)

On user delete, each driver runs `DELETE FROM reaction WHERE creator_id = …` (the user’s own reactions) and `DELETE FROM reaction WHERE content_id IN …` (reactions on that user’s memos). The `reaction` table only has `creator_id INTEGER NOT NULL` plus a uniqueness constraint—no foreign key or `ON DELETE CASCADE`.
